summary.headline: Hi-Tech Pipes Q4 FY26 volume rose 27% to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue rose 102% to INR1,480 crores, while FY27 volume guidance is 6.5-7 lakh tons.
summary.overview: Management reported strong Q4 FY26 volume growth of 27% YoY to 1.47 lakh tons and revenue of INR1,480 crores, up 102% YoY. FY26 volume rose to 5.32 lakh tons from 4.85 lakh tons, and EBITDA grew 8% to INR174 crores. Total comprehensive income in Q4 was INR18 crores against INR17.5 crores a year earlier. Management reiterated a 2 million ton capacity roadmap with 1 million tons to be added by FY29, and the call drew heavy questions on a large stock-in-trade cost line that analysts saw as depressing per-ton margins.

segments.name: Value-added products
segments.commentary: Contribution reached 39% of business mix in FY26; management expects around 50% by end of FY27 as DFT and Hindupur capacity ramp. 300x300 hollow sections were launched during FY26.

segments.name: Stock-in-trade (trading)
segments.commentary: Trading cost was about INR21 crores in Q3 and about INR300 crores in Q4, around INR700 crores across two quarters per the CFO. Management described margins on this as very nominal and said it will decline as the newly operational plants ramp up.

guidance_outlook: FY27 volume target of 6.5-7 lakh tons.
FY28 volume estimate around 8.5 lakh tons, based on 1.4 million tons capacity at 62-65% utilisation (70% peak).
EBITDA per ton of INR3,500-4,000 for FY27 and FY28, assuming no volatility and balanced demand-supply.
Capacity target of around 1.4 million tons by end FY27 and 1.7 million tons exit in FY28; 2 million tons is the longer-term goal, with INR300 crores of capex still needed (INR75-100 crores in FY27).
Value-added share expected to reach around 50% by FY27 end.
capex_capacity: Sanand Unit 2 Phase 3 DFT facility expected operational by Q3 FY27; Sanand APA pipes facility readiness by Q3 FY27 per Q&A (Q4 FY27 per prepared remarks). Oil and gas entry to start with water applications.
Greenfield Hindupur (Andhra Pradesh) facility, about 1.5 lakh tons coated/pre-galvanised/galvanised tubes for solar, expected operational by Q4 FY27; fully integrated for ERW pipes and solar tubes.
Chennai (Sri City) facility on track, expected commissioning in FY27 with full-year benefit in FY28.
FY28 capacity additions: Sanand 1.5 lakh tons, Hindupur 2 lakh tons, Sri City Chennai 1.5 lakh tons, UP plant about 2 lakh tons.
Incremental 1 million ton capex: around INR100 crores already in CWIP; another INR300 crores needed to reach 2 million tons.
Solar capacity 16.5 MW installed, about 35% of power needs; green hydrogen trial started at Secunderabad Unit 1.
demand_pricing: Management cited robust demand across segments including data centres, railways, solar, infrastructure and power projects.
Q4 headwinds: gas price volatility, intermittent gas availability, and elevated ocean freight, creating temporary pressure on input costs and export realisations industry-wide.
Rupee depreciation cited as making Indian exports more competitive; international certifications secured for Europe, America and Middle East.
Management said the stock-in-trade purchases were partly due to geopolitical import cargo and supplier commitment volumes; discounts and rebates would be hit if volumes were not lifted.

qa_highlights.question: Purpose and pricing of the INR90 crore preferential issue to promoters (individual investor).
qa_highlights.answer: Anish Bansal said the INR90 crore issue is by promoters and funds the working capital needs of the 1 million to 2 million ton expansion. No issue price was given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: What products Hindupur will make and the FY27 volume guidance.
qa_highlights.answer: Hindupur is a coated steel tube facility of about 1.5 lakh tons, making coated, pre-galvanised and galvanised tubes mainly for solar. FY27 volume target is 6.5-7 lakh tons.

qa_highlights.question: Greenfield vs brownfield split of the extra 1 million tons.
qa_highlights.answer: Sanand is brownfield and Hindupur greenfield, a 50:50 split; capacity reaches about 1.4 million tons by end FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Timeline and approvals for oil and gas (API) pipes.
qa_highlights.answer: Full readiness of the Sanand API unit expected by Q3 FY27 after 1.5 years of equipment installation and testing. Start with water applications, then migrate to oil and gas, with export potential.

qa_highlights.question: Stock-in-trade cost jump and its margins; whether trading continues.
qa_highlights.answer: Stock-in-trade cost was about INR700 crores across Q3 and Q4 per the CFO, covering HRC, CR and galvanised products, with very nominal margins. Management said trading will fall as three newly operational plants (Secunderabad, Gujarat, Jammu) ramp up, and that stock was sold in March to avoid price-volatility losses.

qa_highlights.question: Capex breakdown and FY28 capacity and volume.
qa_highlights.answer: About INR100 crores is in CWIP and INR300 crores more is needed; INR75-100 crores targeted for FY27. FY28 capacity exit about 1.7 million tons, volume around 8.5 lakh tons, EBITDA per ton INR3,500-4,000.

risks_watch: Stock-in-trade purchases (about INR700 crores across Q3-Q4) depress gross margin and per-ton profitability; the company says this will fall as new plants ramp up.
Q4 EBITDA margin per ton (INR3,150) is well below the FY28 guidance of INR3,500-4,000, which assumes stable markets.
Execution risk on Hindupur (Q4 FY27), Chennai (FY27 commissioning), DFT (Q3 FY27) and API readiness (Q3 FY27), with the 2 million ton target spread into FY29.
Energy input costs, gas availability and ocean freight remain volatile.
Transcript inconsistencies (FY26 revenue base, Q4 EBITDA comparison, APA timeline Q3 vs Q4 FY27) should be checked against the filed results.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume growth, capacity roadmap and value-added mix, but noticeably less forthcoming on the stock-in-trade cost surge, which was addressed only briefly and with shifting explanations. Guidance is stated firmly, with FY28 EBITDA per ton of INR3,500-4,000 conditional on no market volatility.
key_quotes: So, by FY27, our share of value-added products will be almost 50% by end of this year because the capacity for DFT and this Hindupur facility are mainly into value-added segment.
So, if the markets and all, if there is no volatility and if the markets are aligned, the demand and supply, so about INR3,500 to INR4,000 is a very comfortable number.
And March was a month of extreme volatility and extreme uncertainty. So, we did not want to incur any loss on the price volatility. So, it was best to get rid of stock.
